transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-05-04
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Marina Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Hawthorne Head of ML), Michael O'Neal (Lead Data Eng), Sara Kim (PM)

Summary (auto):
00:00 - Marina opens, quick intros and goals; 00:04 - Diego shares demo plan: Prompt sets -> Regression alerts -> A/B bakeoff; 00:50 - Deep dive into console, telemetry and result metrics; 01:05 - Discussed security (SOC2, VPC) and pilot logistics; 01:15 - Recap + next steps.

Topics covered: prompt curation, how regression alerts are triggered, split traffic/AB mechanics, thresholding, baseline benchmarking, sample artifact links.

Action items (captured): Marina to send pilot docs, Diego to run baseline benchmark and share CSV, Priya to export 1000 sample requests.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Marina: hey everyone, uh thanks for joining — I'm Marina Chen from Redwood, i run the account, and with me is Diego our solutions engineer.
[00:15] Priya: hi thanks, Priya Shah here. we, um, are excited to see how you catch regressions — we've had one or two surprises during model swaps.
[00:22] Diego: yeah absolutely, that's kind of the bread and butter for our Eval tooling. today i'll walk through prompt sets, how you define tests, then alerts, and finally an A/B bakeoff flow in the console and API.
[00:40] Michael: quick note on our side — our platform is event-driven, we run inference across multiple models and sometimes route by cost. latency matters but accuracy is main KPI.
[00:49] Marina: perfect. goal for 45 minutes demo, 15 minutes Q&A, and leave with a pilot scope. sound good?
[00:55] Sara: yep works.
[01:05] Diego: ok jumping in, so first — prompt sets. the idea is you assemble a representative set of prompts and expected outputs, can be open or closed form. you then run those across model variants and compare metrics like exact match, entailment, and custom rubrics.
[01:25] Priya: do you support fuzzy matching? sometimes our responses can be semantically equal but lexically different.
[01:30] Diego: yeah we have multiple scorers — BLEU-like, embedding-similarity, and custom python scoring via our eval SDK. we call out semantic drift and give a composite score. small note: the embedding sim is sometimes labeled as "embed-sim" in the console, sorry for inconsistency in the label, we'll fix that.
[01:48] Marina: (laughs) lovely, roadmap note noted.
[01:54] Diego: next — regression alerts. you define a baseline (usually last production model) and thresholds for each metric. when a new model's score drops beyond the threshold, the system fires an alert and can open a runbook entry.
[02:10] Michael: are those alerts integrated with our PagerDuty?
[02:12] Diego: yes, via webhook and Slack, also email. we can also push events to your observability pipeline.
[02:18] Priya: what's the expected false positive rate — like how noisy are these alerts?
[02:22] Diego: great question — defaults are conservative: usually 3-sigma for statistical alarms. but you can tune per prompt-group. we also provide an A/B comparison to validate whether a drop is meaningful to users.
[02:40] Marina: i'm going to share a deck link in chat with example thresholds and the benchmark template.
[02:45] Sara: got it.
[02:50] Diego: moving into the console — i'll share my screen. you can define prompt sets either by uploading CSV or via API. here's an example prompt set for a fulfillment-prediction flow — we tag prompts by intent and expected label.
[03:10] Priya: can we link prompts to specific routes in our service? we have different endpoints for ETA vs pickup.
[03:15] Diego: yes, we support metadata tags and route-level mapping; when you send requests via Redwood API you can include route tags so results join back to prompt group.
[03:25] Michael: and KV cache effects — if we have cached prefixes, will that distort the benchmark?
[03:29] Diego: good point — benchmarking runs can be set to cold-start mode which bypasses prefix cache and also a production-like mode that mirrors your traffic. we show both.
[03:40] Marina: pause — Priya, what's your immediate concern? accuracy drop, latency regressions, cost changes, or all three?
[03:48] Priya: mainly accuracy and silent regressions after model retrain. latency is secondary. cost we watch but can tolerate some uplift if quality gains.
[03:56] Diego: ok so we'll focus alerts on classification/regression metrics, plus a composite to capture semantic drift.
[04:05] Diego: next up, A/B bakeoff. you can spin up an experiment that splits traffic between model A and model B or run a shadow test. Redwood will collect per-prompt metrics and produce pairwise comparison charts.
[04:20] Priya: do you support weighted traffic splits and ramping?
[04:23] Diego: yes, 1-100% with time-based ramps and auto-rollbacks if alerts exceed thresholds. we also have a canary rollback playbook you can plug in.
[04:35] Michael: curious about data residency — can we keep logs in our VPC?
[04:38] Marina: for Private deployments we keep telemetry inside your VPC and integrate with customer KMS. for hosted we're SOC 2 compliant and have retention controls; we'll share the SOC 2 report.
[04:50] Priya: ok would need to see the network diagram and KMS policies.
[04:54] Marina: yes we'll add that to the follow-ups.
[05:00] Diego: demo: here's the 'Compare' view — each prompt shows metric deltas, and you can filter to prompts with >10% drop in semantic-sim. here's where you'd mark a prompt as flakey or update expected output and re-run.
[05:20] Sara: can product folks comment on a prompt and create a task?
[05:23] Diego: yeah each prompt result has a comment thread and task creation that links back to Jira or your issue tracker.
[05:30] Priya: talk me through a failure case — we swapped to a quantized variant and saw consistent hallucinations around SKU codes.
[05:38] Diego: we've seen that — typically quantization can alter tokenization edge cases. our Optimize tooling suggests quantization profiles and flags prompts sensitive to lower precision. in the Compare UI you can see which prompts regress and get recommended mitigations — e.g., keep that prompt pinned to full-precision variant.
[05:58] Marina: we also offer automatic fallback: if the cheaper quantized model emits a high-regression signal for a particular prompt, the router can fallback to the full model for that route.
[06:10] Michael: that could help cost management. what about batch inference — we do nightly bulk scoring.
[06:15] Diego: bulk runs are supported via the API and a job runner; they feed right into the eval dashboard and you can schedule nightly baseline runs.
[06:25] Priya: on the scoring metrics — you mentioned custom rubrics. can I upload a python function?
[06:30] Diego: yes via the eval SDK you can register a scoring function; we sandbox it and run it during evaluation. small caveat: sandboxed run times are limited, we'll share the limits.
[06:45] Marina: quick check — is this consistent with what you expected? are there any blockers for pilot data access?
[06:50] Priya: we can provide sample data but need to strip PII first. we have a transformation job that can do that.
[06:56] Sara: timeline wise, how long to get baseline metrics back?
[07:00] Diego: typically 48-72 hours for a 1k prompt set end-to-end; if we run a quick smoke test we can get initial numbers in 6-8 hours.
[07:10] Priya: cool. show me the alerts UI again?
[07:13] Diego: sure, here's the alert config screen: you choose metric, comparator (absolute, relative), threshold, and scope (global, prompt-group, per-route). you can attach a runbook link and auto-create a ticket.
[07:30] Marina: question — do you want alert noise reduction features like rate-limiting or compound checks?
[07:34] Priya: yes compound checks would be helpful — only alert if both semantic-sim and label-accuracy drop.
[07:40] Diego: we support compound conditions and can set rolling windows (e.g., 30 min).
[07:48] Michael: how are A/B results statistically evaluated? is it bootstrapping?
[07:52] Diego: we run paired significance tests by default with bootstrap CIs. we surface p-values and effect sizes; but we emphasise practical significance and per-prompt impact.
[08:05] Sara: can product set acceptance criteria — like minimal lift thresholds?
[08:08] Diego: yep, acceptance rules can gate rollouts. if you set min lift of X% we won't roll unless it's met.
[08:15] Priya: any constraints on prompt-set size? we have thousands, but we can pick subsets.
[08:19] Diego: no hard limit; UI handles pagination for large sets. for performance we recommend sampling a representative 1-5k.
[08:27] Marina: quick live example — i'm going to upload a tiny CSV. bear with me, i might fumble.
[08:35] Diego: (chuckles) take your time.
[08:40] Marina: ok uploaded, you should see 'hawthorne-eta-sample.csv' in the workspace.
[08:46] Priya: yes i see it.
[08:48] Diego: great, running evaluation now — starting baseline against model X-2027 and candidate Y-quant.
[08:56] (sound of typing)
[09:10] Diego: initial results — candidate shows 12% drop on semantic-sim for prompts tagged 'sku-match'. consoles sometimes abbreviate labels as 'sem-sim' so ignore that mismatch in visual.
[09:24] Priya: that's similar to what we saw internally. can we drill down to the raw responses?
[09:28] Diego: yep — dropping into a single prompt, you can view both outputs, token-by-token diff, and a short explanation from our comparator. it also highlights hallucinated tokens.
[09:40] Michael: this is actually really useful for our devs to triage.
[09:44] Marina: ok moving on — pilot scope. recommended: 1k canonical prompts, two model variants, baseline run and A/B 2-week test on 5% traffic.
[09:56] Priya: 5% ramp seems reasonable. would rather start 1% and ramp to 5% though.
[10:00] Marina: nod, we'll set a ramp.
[10:03] Diego: one final note on integrations: we support SSO/SAML, role-based access, and audit logs; for Private customers we also map to KMS.
[10:15] Priya: perfect. any compliance concerns?
[10:18] Marina: for hosted we provide SOC 2, ISO summary on request; for more sensitive needs we have Private deployments where telemetry never leaves your VPC.
[10:28] Michael: fine. what's pricing look like for this pilot?
[10:31] Marina: i'll follow up with a pilot quote — usually a time-boxed evaluation fee plus usage credits. i'll include estimated token costs in the spreadsheet.
[10:40] Sara: will you also share the benchmark template?
[10:42] Marina: yes sending shortly.
[10:45] (short pause)
[10:50] Priya: couple more quick questions — can we do on-prem air-gapped testing?
[10:55] Diego: yes, our on-prem package supports air-gapped environments; there are some setup windows but we've done it with two logistics customers before.
[11:05] Priya: thanks. also curious about automation for prompt fixes — can Redwood suggest prompt rewrites?
[11:10] Diego: we have a suggestions engine that proposes minimal rewrites and ranks them by expected lift. it's experimental but helpful as a starting point.
[11:20] Marina: ok wrapping up. recap: customer to provide prompt set + sample requests (Priya), Redwood runs baseline and shares spreadsheet (Diego), Marina sends pilot doc + pricing + SOC2 (Marina). quick kickoff next week (May 10).
[11:40] Priya: thanks all. excited to try the bakeoff.
[11:44] Marina: great — we'll follow up in the next 24 hours with artifacts. thanks everyone.
[11:50] Michael: thanks. bye.

End of transcript."
